title: Hybrid rollout observability readiness checklist
content:
Context and intention

This is a practical, checklist-first doc for preparing observability during hybrid model rollouts: when traffic is split between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Goal: make rollouts predictable for latency/cost/quality, reduce operator cognitive load, and ensure measurable rollback/upgrade decision points. Not a cookbook for instrumentation itself — assume standard metric/tracing libs are available — but a readiness runbook for release engineers, SRE, and product owners before flip.

Status notes to reviewers
- Draft: focus on pragmatic tests we can run end-to-end (synthetic probes + production slices)
- Requesting input from network/security on private deployment trace egress constraints
- Ask: should we standardize a single dashboard template per model family for hybrid rollouts?

High-level checklist (pre-rollout gating)
1) Ownership and communication- Document primary signal owners (latency, cost, error rate, model-quality) and secondary contacts for hosted/dedicated/private variants 
- Confirm Slack channels + escalation rotation updated for rollout window

2) Metric & SLI alignment- Ensure uniform SLI definitions across deployment types. If a metric differs in implementation (e.g., agent-side sampling on private installations), add alias mapping in metric catalog.
- Required SLIs: p50/p90/p99 tail latency (inference pipeline), tokens-per-second throughput (per GPU pool), request error rate (5xx/timeout), model-quality regression score (prompt-set eval), kv-cache-warmth ratio (hit/miss), billing-rate (tokens/sec and estimated $/hr).
- SLO gating thresholds for rollout: set conservative SLOs for first 24–72 hours with automatic escalation points. Example: p99 < 600ms for hosted, p99 < 900ms for dedicated (configurable), and p99 < 1200ms for private; error rate < 0.5% for all.

3) Tracing contract and propagation checks- Confirm trace headers and span naming match across proxies/service mesh/edge runtimes. We must be able to join traces that begin in hosted control plane and continue into private on-prem adapters.- Verify trace context propagation over encrypted/private links: sampling decisions must be preserved (inject traceparent).- Create at least three test traces that exercise: (a) host->model fanout across variants, (b) fallback to cheaper model variant, (c) KV cache cold-start path. Label test traces with rollout_tag:{rollout-id}.

4) Dashboard & quickcards- Create or duplicate a rollout dashboard with consolidated tiles for: SLI status, latency distribution by deployment type, model-quality by variant, tenant-weighted cost forecast, active request routing map, KV cache warmth heatmap, and sample traces list.- Add operator quickcards (click-to-run) for common investigation queries: top n slow requests (by tenant), traces with fallback=true, worst-performing prompt-sets, cost anomaly query.

5) Sampling and trace cost mitigation- Define adaptive sampling policy for rollout window: increase sampling for rollout-tagged requests and model-quality check traces; reduce baseline sampling elsewhere to keep trace cost neutral.- Implement trace retention tiers: high-fidelity traces for first 48 hours (rollout-tagged), compact traces (span-level metadata only) for 48–7 days, aggregated breadcrumbs for 7+ days.

6) Synthetic probes and end-to-end smoke tests- Author probes that exercise the slowest code path (long sequence length + heavy context). Run probes simultaneously against hosted/dedicated/private endpoints and compare p95/p99 and tokens/sec.- Validate probe outputs for semantic similarity (basic quality sanity) against golden prompt sets. Flag if similarity drops beyond threshold.

7) Cost and query budget controls- Precompute per-minute and per-hour cost burn estimates for rollout traffic split scenarios (10/30/60% to new variant). Add budget alarms that will raise if projected hourly spend exceeds accepted limit.- Lock query-cardinality (dashboard queries) with query timeouts and sample-limited joins to prevent thundering queries during investigation.

8) Rollout-specific logs and metadata- Ensure every request routed to new variant includes: rollout_tag, variant_id, customer_tier, tenant_id (or tenant_hash), and routing_reason. These must be present in logs/metrics/traces for end-to-end stitching.- Add a small structured payload sample store (redacted) for failed quality checks to aid RLHF/debugging without leaking PII.

9) Runbooks and automated fallback triggers- Define automated fallback triggers and safe rollback conditions (examples): sustained p99 > X ms for 10 minutes AND error_rate > Y% OR model-quality drop > Z on golden set.- Document manual runbook steps for rollback: reversion command, state sync for kv-cache, and customer notification template.

10) Post-rollout validation and sprintback- 24-hour, 72-hour, and 7-day checks: latency/cost/quality deltas, incident review, dashboard fatigue analysis, and signal adjustments.- Capture metric drift and instrumentation gaps that appeared only during hybrid traffic (e.g., missing tenant tags from private proxies) and open tickets.

Detailed instrumentation notes and gotchas
- Tenant tagging across private deployments: Some private customers deploy a sidecar that strips certain headers. Add fallback tenant_hash derived from auth token as a defensive tag. Document the privacy tradeoff and opt-out mechanics.
- KV cache metrics: Count both per-pool miss rate and cross-pool eviction churn.- Clock skew: Private deployments sometimes have misaligned clocks causing trace ordering issues. For traces that cross machines, prefer monotonic span timestamps where possible and store both wall-clock and monotonic offsets.
- Network egress policies: Private deployments behind strict egress policies may block trace export. Provide a verification script that checks trace export endpoints and TLS certs. Include fallback: local aggregation buffer with burst export to control plane.

Investigation query snippets (operator-friendly)
- Top slow tenants in last 15m by p99 latency: group by tenant_hash and deployment_type, sort desc.- Traces with fallback and long-kv-latency: span tags: fallback=true AND kv_latency_ms > 50.- Model-quality regressions: daily prompt-set baseline similarity by variant_id, show change pct.

Preflight automation tasks (CI/CD hooks)
- Automated smoke-run against a canary tenant cluster after infra commit. Fails CI if p99 increases > 20% vs baseline.
- Validate that dashboard queries compile within query-time budgets (example: < 6s).

Postmortem and signal improvement cadence
- For every rollback or major alert triggered by rollout, require a one-pager that covers: what signal tripped, why instrumentation failed (if it did), who was paged, remediation, and recommended metric contract updates.
- Monthly signal grooming session to prune noisy panels introduced during rollouts.

Open questions / TODOs
- Should we require the same sampling library/config across private and hosted by default? Tradeoff: private customers may object to outgoing telemetry.
- Need a compact onboarding script for private customers to validate trace export without exposing customer data.
- Decide canonical naming for rollout_tag values and where they live (release pipeline vs. runtime injection).

Appendix: rollout-template quick checklist (one-line items for runbook)
- Create rollout_id and tag in release job- Duplicate rollout dashboard and pin to oncall view- Ensure synthetic probes scheduled and baseline recorded- Verify trace headers pass through network path- Confirm SLO thresholds and budget alarms set- Estimate burn for 10/30/60% traffic splits and set cost alarms- Preflight smoke-run for canary tenant cluster- Notify stakeholders and set escalation schedule- Start rollout with small percentage and monitor 0/5/30/120 minute gates- Execute post-rollout reviews at 24h/72h/7d

Notes to self
- Keep this doc short and actionable; link to deeper instrumentation guides elsewhere.
- After first hybrid rollout in Q1, convert the appendix to a checklist in Confluence with automation links.

End of doc.
